# React Gotchas

> Known React patterns that cause infinite loops, memory leaks, or silent state bugs. Load all HIGH entries before writing React components.

## Entries

- [useEffect infinite loop when state setter depends on its own state](useeffect-infinite-loop.md): Calling setState inside useEffect with that state in the dependency array creates an infinite re-render loop. HIGH.
- [setTimeout in useEffect without cleanup fires after unmount](settimeout-cleanup.md): setTimeout scheduled in useEffect fires even after unmount, updating stale state. Always return a cleanup function. MEDIUM.
- [base-ui Select shows the raw value in its collapsed trigger without an items prop](base-ui-select-items-prop-collapsed-trigger.md): Children-only SelectItem labels don't resolve before mount or for values missing from the mounted list, so the trigger silently shows raw enums/ids; always pass items={[{value,label}]} and resolve labels for stale values. MEDIUM.
- [Unmount flush resurrects localStorage state cleared by another component](unmount-flush-resurrects-cleared-state.md): An autosave hook's flush-on-unmount re-saves a draft another component just cleared (discard then navigate unmounts AFTER the clear); pair the external clear with an event that makes the flush a no-op. MEDIUM.
- [react-hooks/set-state-in-effect is an ERROR, breaking post-fetch state reconciliation](set-state-in-effect-is-an-error.md): Recent eslint-plugin-react-hooks presets ship the rule at error severity, and it matches lexically: it flags any component-scope function containing setState when called from an effect (even fully-async loaders that cannot cascade) while accepting an async IIFE that genuinely does. Move reconciliation into the fetch callback; use render-phase adjustment for the reset-on-dep-change family. The identity-stable updater trick does NOT silence it. MEDIUM.
- [Clearing react-hooks/immutability by hoisting a fetcher unmasks set-state-in-effect](immutability-hoist-unmasks-set-state-in-effect.md): Hoisting a fetcher above the effect to fix "Cannot access variable before it is declared" is what finally lets set-state-in-effect resolve the binding, so it starts erroring on a line you never touched; the originally-reported errors go away while the file still fails lint. It reports only once per effect (first offending call), and neither moving setState out of `finally` nor deleting a synchronous pre-await setState silences it. MEDIUM.
- [A hook returning a ref inside its result object makes every property read of that object a ref access](hook-returning-ref-in-object-flags-every-read.md): The compiler marks the whole returned object as a ref, so `style={resize.styleVars}` and every other plain read in the CALLER's JSX errors with "Cannot access refs during render" while the message never names the offending property; often masked behind a more obvious violation, so it materialises only after you fix that one. Have the caller own the ref and pass it in. MEDIUM.
